# Factory Functions

A reusable function library for checking, preparing and inserting child documents from a configured template. It also inherits party mapping, bootstrap preparation, source binding, access registration and activation helpers. It declares no factory trigger or invoking actor; the enclosing workflow determines when these functions run and who may invoke them.

## Checking and creating a child

`checkCreation(input)` requires a nonempty text `key` containing neither `/` nor `~`. The destination is `bindings.collection` followed by that key. It constructs a `creationIntent` containing the template identity, `fields`, `values`, `requestId`, `inheritChannels`, `partyBindings` and `sourcePaths`. Missing `fields` and `values` default to `{}`; `requestId` defaults to `key`. The intent uses empty defaults for unspecified channel inheritance, party mappings and source paths.

If the destination already exists, its `creationIntent` must match exactly. A match returns `outcome: duplicate`; a mismatch fails with `DOCUMENT_KEY_CONFLICT`. An unused destination returns `outcome: acceptedNew`, together with `key`, `path` and `intent`. This check neither inserts nor reserves a document.

`constructDocument(checked, input)` prepares and returns the child without inserting it. `create(checked, input)` calls that constructor, appends an addition at `checked.path`, emits a Domain Event with `kind: Document Started`, `clause`, `entityId` and `path`, and returns `acceptedNew`. It does not itself rerun `checkCreation`, handle its duplicate branch or call `configureSources`. A committed insertion does not establish child initialization, activation, external publication or completed bootstrap.

## Template and value configuration

`configurationParameters()` reads the connection configuration's `parameters`, defaulting to `{}`. `configuredTemplate()` prefers `parameters.template`; otherwise it uses the connection's `template` snapshot. `configuredTemplateValue(path)` instead reads the actual template location: `/clauses/{clauseKey}/parameters/template` when that parameter is configured, or `bindings.template` otherwise. Configuration and snapshot functions require implementations supplied by the enclosing execution context.

The constructor rejects a template with `contracts.initialized` already present. Its configurable inputs are:

- `fields`: top-level replacements restricted to `allowedFields`. Even if listed there, these names are forbidden: `contracts`, `clauses`, `type`, `itemType`, `keyType`, `valueType`, `value`, `items`, `blueId`, `blue`, `schema`, `constraints`, `mergePolicy`, `properties`, `$previous`, `$previousItems`, `$pos`, `$replace`, `$empty` and `instanceKey`.
- `values`: named replacements resolved through `fieldPaths`. Each mapping must be text naming an existing constraint slot. The path must start with `/`; its first segment cannot be empty or one of `contracts`, `clauses`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `sources`, `type`, `blueId`, `instanceKey`, `creationIntent` or `preparationContext`. The supplied value is validated against the existing slot before replacement. Unknown names, reserved paths and missing slots fail.
- `inheritChannels`: parent contract names to copy. Names must be nonempty text without `/` or `~`, and each selected contract must be an External Channel or Timeline Channel. A different channel already present under that name in the template causes rejection.
- `sourcePaths`: source aliases mapped to document locations. Construction requires each referenced source to have `contracts.initialized` and places an exact document reference under the child's `sources`.
- `identityChildren`: paths to existing, uninitialized child templates that receive derived identities. Missing or initialized children fail.

The new `instanceKey` is deterministic from the enclosing document's original initialization identity, `clauseKey` and `key`, using `clauseRuntime.initialDocument` when the initialized original is unavailable. Each `identityChildren` entry receives an identity derived from that key and its path. Construction also records `creationIntent` and replaces `sources` with the configured references.

## Parties and bootstrap preparation

A nonempty `bindings.parties` selects explicit mapping through `prepareMappedChild`. Each child role must be mapped unless listed in `suppliedParties`; supplied roles remain declarations and cannot also have mappings. A mapping selects either a parent role or an explicit Party value satisfying the child's declaration. Every parent main identity must remain represented. Main identity checks require matching lead channels and equal, nonempty, duplicate-free reader-key sets. Mapping grants neither access nor consent.

Ordinary mapped preparation requires an uninitialized template with the exact Activation Clause type. It retains the child's activation policy, adds references to parent access documents and installs resolved party transports, rejecting conflicting channels or access locations.

Without a nonempty party mapping, `activateChild` uses `parameters.parties` to select parent roles; an empty or omitted selection means all parent parties. `parameters.readers` selects named parent reader groups and defaults to an empty selection. Unknown roles or readers fail. If the parent has no `activation`, this helper returns the template unchanged. Otherwise it copies parent access references, sets `frozen` to `false`, and preserves the template's `required` list, defaulting that list to `[]` in this construction path.

`prepareFor`, when present, must equal `bootstrap`; this requires `obtain: provide` and an empty `inheritChannels`. Without `prepareFor`, `preparationMode()` returns `inherited`. Bootstrap mapped preparation rejects templates already containing `timelineAccess` or activation `accessPaths`, and removes mapped lead and representative channels while retaining the remaining party information. It prepares transport slots; it does not perform bootstrap.

Inherited bootstrap validation checks retained actors, reader-key sets and representative identities against the expected parties. It also checks initialized access documents, transport coverage and access-path shape, with a separate allowance for admitted-party access paths. Pinned reader declarations containing `myosAccountId` must contain exactly that nonempty account identifier and `readerKeys` with one nonempty key; validation requires the resulting reader groups to match the original publication, clause parameters and activation state.

## Source and access setup

`configureSources(checked, prepared)` first adds a Document Access Clause. Its generated `registerAccess_<role>` workflows use each prepared activation party's channel and accept one to sixteen initialized Timeline Access documents. Existing `documentAccess`, `documentSources` or generated source-observation clause names are rejected when the corresponding helper needs to install them.

Source configuration has two distinct branches:

- Nonempty `sourcePaths` cannot coexist with nonempty legacy `bindings.sources`. Every declared source must have a path, an initialized process origin and a matching declaration. An observation clause embeds each declared source. This branch does not impose the legacy branch's explicit `activation.active` check.
- Legacy `bindings.sources` must have exactly as many entries as the declarations. Aliases must be declared, nonempty and contain none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Each binding is text: `self` selects the enclosing document; other values select a document location. Sources must have an initialized origin, be active and match their declarations. The helper records immutable origin requirements, clears the prepared `sources`, and adds `bindSource_<role>` workflows. For `self`, it also records the new child's selection path.

The base `configuredSources` and `sourceDeclarationMatches` functions fail with `SOURCE_VALIDATOR_NOT_COMPILED`. Declaration-aware source configuration therefore requires specialized implementations.

Inherited `bindSource` accepts a declared `alias` and either `document` or `sourcePath`; a nonempty `sourcePath` takes precedence. It requires the configured original process identity, an active source and coverage of the receiving document's main parties. An existing binding to that origin returns `duplicate`; rebinding to another origin is forbidden. `refreshSourceReadiness` records whether all required sources are initialized, retain their expected origins, are active and cover the receiving roster. A `self` requirement additionally needs the selected child to be initialized with the receiving document's origin. Readiness changes emit Source Readiness Changed; source readiness does not replace commercial acceptance.

Access registration requires exact-document review and a party-lead channel. It validates Timeline Access type, initialization, provider history and the expected executable permission policy. New original access-document identities are embedded and registered for activation refresh; already registered identities return `duplicate`. Registration does not change provider-owned permission lists. Access checking treats reader keys as alternatives within each group; each Timeline Channel needs a matching access document covering its timeline and at least one key from every required group. External Channels bypass this matching check.

## Inherited lifecycle behavior

The inherited activation helpers maintain the enclosing document's `activation` state when invoked. `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` means access is missing before any activation; `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` means it is missing after a previous activation. `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` means access is available but required approvals or current agreed terms are missing. `ACTIVE` requires access, acceptance and an open document; `CLOSED` takes precedence. `everActivated` retains whether activation has ever occurred.

`approve` requires exact-document review, a party-lead channel, the current `revision`, valid access and any required matching `termsRef`. Repeated approval is harmless. Party updates require an unfrozen roster and its lead's authority; adding a role also requires `allowNewParties`. Successful updates validate access, advance the revision and clear approvals. Admission has separate policy and revision checks. These helpers do not make every representative eligible for lead-only operations.

`initializeTerms` records the terms identity and initializes `termsRevision` and negotiation state. Activation can freeze negotiation, and changes to parties or required approvers update the terms identity and close a pending proposal. The inherited amendment helpers separately enforce editable state, allowed paths, revision checks, proposal-ID consistency and configured approvers; they apply a replacement only after all required approvals, emitting Amendment Proposed and Amendment Applied at their respective stages.

State belongs to the document in which a helper executes. Missing recorded state is unknown; initialization defaults apply only after initialization runs.
